releases.headline: A Home built around your jobs, a Work view with the board beside the thread, credits charged by tier, jobs that check in before they spend more, and the Nectovia Agent on your own Personal work with credits you buy.

sections.title: New
items: Home is built around your jobs. Its rail lists Needs your input, Working and Finished, each with its count, and a row opens that job's thread, decision or card. When the business has more than one project, a line at the top of the rail switches between All projects and each project. The ask box sits under the greeting, over the newest exchange, and Earlier opens the rest of the conversation.

Home shows up to two tasks a Nectovia run proposed and left in the Inbox, newest first. Accept moves a task to the Board, where it starts only when you start it, and Not now hides it on this computer.

Home and the Nectovia thread pin the newest bar, line or area chart a reply carried, with a caption saying when it was written. While a step runs, a line sweeps along the chart's baseline, and it stays still when reduced motion is on.

Once the Nectovia conversation has started, Home's ask box has a thread's row in place of the Style box: Engine, Model or tier, Effort and Agent. Its Engine menu lists the AI tools a conversation can run on.

The Agent menu no longer grays out every worker when the conversation is on the Nectovia Agent. Only workers that lead with Build or Fix are grayed, and they say why: the Nectovia Agent doesn't take those modes yet.

A project's top bar has a switch, Nectovia | Work. Work replaces Architect, and a project you kept in Architect opens in Work. The view choice left the ··· menu, and Settings, Appearance and Ctrl K name the two views the same way.

In Work, the board sits beside the thread: Needs your input, Working, Up next and Finished today, under the open count and Open full board. A card opens its thread, and a decision opens where it waits. The thread's own Team and Loop run stay at the top of that column, and Activity and Recent are no longer in it.

On the free version, projects open in Work and the Nectovia tab shows a lock. It opens a short notice with Sign up for a plan, Remind me later and Don't remind me again. The view you chose before is kept, and it comes back with a plan.

Automations are called Routines everywhere you read them, the rail, Everything, Ctrl K and Settings included. Routines is one of the rail's default pins, and on the free version its row says Paid plans.
The team view stays on every plan. On the free version you lead the team, and Nectovia's seat shows that it can lead it on a plan.

Without a plan, you can buy credits and use the Nectovia Agent on your own Personal work while they last. In Personal, Settings, Usage shows the credits you bought and a buy box that buys for you alone. The free version's notice says you can buy credits. Leading a team, Routines and a Nectovia worker or advisor in a loop still need a plan. When the credits run out, work stops at the end of the step in progress and keeps what it did.
In a business with no plan, the Nectovia Agent still needs a plan, and owners and admins are told so wherever they start it. The buy box there says the credits wait for a plan.

Nectovia Agent work is charged in credits at the rate for its tier: Efficient, Focused or Thorough. The rates come from a credit price table Nectovia publishes, and they're the same whichever model does the work. A job's estimate before it starts uses them too.

Jobs check in instead of stopping at a cap. When a job reaches its check-in amount, it finishes the step in progress, saves, and asks whether to keep going. Keep going lets that one job use the same amount again, and Stop here keeps what it did. A loop that reaches its amount waits in Needs you, where Keep going starts it again.

Nectovia's check-in amounts are 100 credits for Efficient, 250 for Focused and 500 for Thorough. Owners and admins can set their business's own amounts in Settings, Usage, under Job check-ins, and a change applies to jobs that start after it.

sections.title: Fixed
items: A loop run waiting to pick up where it left off no longer starts working while Nectovia closes. It picks up the next time Nectovia opens.

sections.title: Updating
items: Settings > App updates offers stable releases only. Nothing is downloaded, verified or installed until you confirm it, and a download is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the digest the release publishes. An installed 0.1.7, 0.1.8, 0.1.9, 0.1.10, 0.1.11, 0.2.0, 0.2.1 or 0.2.3 on Windows can find this release when you press Check for updates.

An update from 0.1.9, 0.1.10, 0.1.11, 0.2.0, 0.2.1 or 0.2.3 keeps your settings, routes, saved keys, projects and conversations. An update from 0.1.7 or 0.1.8 that skips 0.1.9 still gets the one-time fresh start 0.1.9 introduced: the earlier version's data and the Documents\Diomedes folder are set aside, renamed with "before 0.1.9" and the date, and nothing is deleted.

Your install is refreshed the first time this version opens, and again after each later update. Settings you never changed move to the new defaults, anything you chose is kept, cached screens are cleared, and a byte-for-byte backup and a record of what moved are kept. A custom look keeps its colours, fonts and artwork, while text sizes, line spacing and density follow the new version. You see it once: Updated to 0.2.4, with how many settings moved.

Saving AI routing and privacy settings needs 0.2.3 or later, because the account service no longer accepts them from 0.2.1. A choice saved in 0.2.1 keeps working under its earlier rules until you save it again.
This release has no Mac build. A Mac keeps the version it has, and Check for updates there doesn't offer this Windows release.

sections.title: Known limits
items: This build is unsigned and experimental. On Windows, SmartScreen may warn before the installer runs: choose More info, then Run anyway, after checking the file's SHA-256.

Settings > Account and the Nectovia Agent's AI service were tested only against stand-ins for the Nectovia account service. A real sign-in has run on one installed Windows copy of a test build made before 0.2.3. Two sign-in fixes came after it: finishing without a second press, and the page the browser tab ends on. Both were tested only against stand-ins. The account service this version uses is still a staging service with a fixed testing budget: while it is, the Nectovia Agent's answers are kept short, and the Agent stops answering once that budget is spent.

The account service hasn't published models or credit prices for any tier yet. Until it does, work on a Nectovia tier is refused with a note that the tier has no Nectovia model right now, and nothing is charged. Work on your own AI tools isn't affected.

The page in the browser tab needs port 47319 on your computer. If another program is using that port, the tab stays on a loading bar as before, and sign-in still finishes in the app. If you quit Nectovia before you finish in the browser, the browser says it can't connect. Open Nectovia and sign in again.
The Norton change was checked with Norton on one Windows computer. Other antivirus programs weren't tried.

Signing in needs the Nectovia account service, so if it can't be reached when Nectovia starts, you can't open anything, your own projects included; the sign-in screen says why. A connection lost after you sign in doesn't sign you out.

Buying credits isn't available yet. Until payments are set up on the account service, Settings, Usage answers that buying isn't available right now, and buying has run only against a stand-in payment service. Pay as you go can't be used until then.

Once buying opens, credits you buy without a plan run the Nectovia Agent in Home's conversation. This version still shows you Nectovia locked in the Nectovia | Work switch and grayed in the Engine menu.

Pay as you go, credit prices, check-ins, credit limits, bought credits, Individual credits and the paid-access changes were tested against stand-ins and test databases, not against the live account service.
This version has no screen for setting a member's monthly limit. Unless one is set, a member's limit is the plan's whole allowance.
When an Individual plan ends, Personal Agent work is refused, but the default conversation doesn't move back to your own AI tool the way a business's does.
A routine that reaches its check-in amount waits in Needs you without Keep going. Start it again to go on.
Routines has a New routine button that can't be used yet.
Under All projects, when the business has more than one project, Home shows no suggestions and no Finished group.

The new account routing has not yet completed a real signed-in, paid-provider acceptance run. Automated routing tests use synthetic model responses. A route without current qualification or required privacy consent stays unavailable.
Apart from a few conversation turns on one outside engine and a connection check on the company's AI account, nothing in this version was tried against a real provider.
Board work on the Nectovia Agent, including work a request starts in Automatic mode, was tested with stand-in model responses only. Helpers and teams don't run on it.
Team cards and hand-offs were tested with stand-in tools only.

The phone apps can't reach this computer through the relay yet; this version only connects the computer and lists it as online. The relay was tested against a stand-in and hasn't yet run on the live account service.
An update that installs this version over an earlier one, including the change from Diomedes.exe to nectovia.exe, hasn't been run on an installed copy.
Routines run the weekly brief alone, and only while this computer is on. They tell you inside the app and send nothing by push, email or phone.
Resume, Retry, Fork and Steer work on Codex runs only.
Run checks run only the checks a task declares, and never run your project's own code. Nothing checks a run automatically when it finishes.
Files has no PDF viewer. Pictures and PDFs cannot be sent to an AI, and a binary file cannot be put back from an earlier version.

Trigger rules don't watch conversations, Ask or Plan. Tool rules don't reach Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or other outside tools, which run their own tools, and on every outside tool except Codex a text rule reads the text after secrets are removed, so a rule looking for a secret may not fire there. A correction asked of a tool other than Codex was not tested, and a rule that asks a work loop run to correct still can't reach it: the correction is recorded and shown as not sent.

Delegates that change files in their own copy, and a lead that runs a team of them on your own connected services, are built but can't be started from the app yet, though the Loop run dialog can now add a Nectovia worker and advisor. The Console still has no History screen and no Make tasks from this plan.

Every route except the Nectovia Agent still runs on, and is billed to, your own account. A provider connection you saved yourself works only for a business whose plan includes the Nectovia Agent, or for Personal work on an Individual plan. You can still choose such a connection for a thread, and Settings has no place to change or remove it.
The local model needs a server that answers llama.cpp's props request, so Nectovia can tell which profile is running. Without it the model shows as running, and work that names a profile is refused.

Prompt caching and the route checks were built and tested against stand-ins. No call reached a provider while building them, so whether a provider honors Off shows only in a route check on your own connection.
The local model can't be chosen for a Team member or a loop run from the app yet.

The Nectovia worker and advisor in the Loop run dialog were tested only against stand-ins, a scripted local model server and the offline scripted account service, never a live Nectovia tier or the live account service.

releases.headline: A free version beside paid plans, a model on your own computer that can hand work to Nectovia, a Team of your own AI tools on the Board, a Usage section with member credit limits, paid Automations and a repaired Windows sign-in.

sections.title: New
items: Nectovia has a free version. Without a paid plan you keep your projects, files and workspace, the task board, conversations and work on your own AI tools, and your projects' own instruction files. The Nectovia Agent, its included usage, Business rules, Automations and phone access come with a paid plan. A notice says when you're on the free version, and Settings > Account shows your plan.
Supported conversation engines keep their own sessions across follow-up messages, Stops and restarts. When an engine supplies a thinking summary, the conversation can show it above the reply.

Settings has a Usage section. Owners and admins see the business's Agent usage this month, the credits it bought and what's reserved for work in flight, and a place to buy more. A member sees their own use against their own monthly limit. The usage panel warns when 75 and 90 percent of the monthly allowance is used or reserved, and again when it runs out.
Work that runs out of credits stops at that step and keeps what it already did. An owner or admin is told to buy more in Settings, Usage, and anyone else is told that an owner or admin can buy more.
A member about to pass their monthly credit limit can ask for that one job or for more this month. Owners and admins see the asks under Change workspace and approve or decline each one.
Automations need a paid plan. Without one, their setup and history are kept but nothing runs, and a schedule that was on shows Blocked: needs a paid plan.

When a business's paid access ends, the next Nectovia Agent message is refused with the reason, the default conversation goes back to your own AI tool, and the free version notice returns. When access is granted again, the next message picks it up with no restart.

Personal Agent access and managed usage funding are checked separately. An Individual plan covers Personal work and includes monthly credits, and Settings > Account shows them with the exact time the period ends.

A Board task has a Task permission panel: stop at each phase change or approve the whole task, cap its action turns and pick an optional playbook. Tasks the Nectovia Agent proposes wait in Inbox, and Start on a Board task can run on the Nectovia Agent.

On the Agent page, a project's conversation in Automatic mode can now start work on the Nectovia Agent with no Start click. A request like Fix the price list becomes a Board task set to approve the whole task, with up to 12 action turns. Finished work waits in Review.

Your Team, the AI tools you add in the Team view, can now take Board cards. Assign gives an Inbox, Ready or Blocked card to a member. A card a member makes waits in Inbox and runs on that member's Codex or Claude Code when you start it. Only you move its phase, reassign it or remove it. Teams are part of the free version.

Hand off passes what came of one card to the next member's card, with up to eight changed files, checks and open issues. Starting that card sends those files. The Team view lists what's running and who pays for it.
ChatGPT is now called Codex, after the coding tool it runs through. You still sign in with your ChatGPT account.

The ask box has one row under the message line: the modes, then Engine, Model or tier, Effort and Agent, then Attach, a context ring and Send. The pickers that were in the header moved into it, so each choice shows once.

Nectovia can use a model that runs on this computer. In Settings, set Local model folder to a folder whose nectovia-connection.json describes the model, its server on this computer, its profiles and its own start and stop scripts. The ask row then offers it by the name and context size its running server reports. It starts only when you press Start, a send to a stopped model is refused rather than moved to a cloud model, and local work uses no credits.

When a Loop run is led by one of your own connected services rather than Nectovia, the Loop run dialog can add a Nectovia worker and a Nectovia advisor at the tier you choose, such as Focused or Thorough, and they use your account's credits once you confirm where their work goes. If your account has handing work to Nectovia turned off, for every tier or for one, that tier shows as unavailable with the reason and nothing is sent to it.

AI setup has a Prompt caching setting for your own AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI connections: Provider default, Off or Explicit prefix. Provider default sends requests as before. Beside it, AI setup shows what each model can do and where each fact comes from: a cited page, a route check, or not known.

For your own AWS and Azure connections, AI setup can run route checks on a model: a few small live requests on that connection's key and spend limit, kept as a receipt. Kimi K3 on your AWS connection sends only while a current check covers it.

Settings > Account > AI routing and privacy offers two profiles, with Balanced selected for a new account. Neither uses your content for training, and requests can run outside the US. Balanced prefers providers that don't store your content, then US processing, and Lowest cost uses the least expensive AI that can do the job. Strict keeps requests in the US with no provider storage, and it's available on request at hello@diomedes.net. An account that already chose Strict keeps it. Saving names what a looser choice gives up, and a choice saved under the earlier rules asks to be saved again.

sections.title: Fixed
items: On Windows, signing in no longer stops at a gray screen after you finish in the browser. The app now accepts the sign-in callback in the form Windows hands it.
After you finish in the browser, Nectovia signs you in by itself. You no longer have to press Sign in with your browser a second time.
When sign-in finishes, the browser tab shows a page that says you're signed in and can close it. Before, the tab stayed on a loading bar.
If the account service can't read your plan while you sign in, sign-in still finishes. Free work goes ahead, and Nectovia Agent work is refused until your access can be confirmed.

Home lists the newest three items waiting on you, each with Review or Check, and its links open the task or approval they name. Needs you counts approvals, changes awaiting review and failed work consistently across the Console. Review work is described as needing attention rather than requiring an OK.
Account changes and sign-out cannot restore a stale session or borrow an admission made for another person. Streamed replies and thinking summaries redact secrets split across engine output chunks.
Marking a task Done by hand is refused while a change waits for review or a Need is open.
Windows briefly locking a record or run file no longer fails the save, a run or the weekly brief.
The greeting on Home no longer grows as the window gets wider. Text keeps one size at every window width, and a bigger window adds margin instead.
On Windows, installing OpenCode no longer sets off a Norton antivirus alert. The step that unpacks it now starts Windows PowerShell in a form Norton's behavior check doesn't flag.

releases.headline: You now sign in with a Nectovia account, and the Nectovia Agent answers on Nectovia's own AI service for a business whose plan includes it. Trigger rules also watch task work on every tool, and answers follow one plain-writing standard.

sections.title: New
items: Nectovia now asks you to sign in with a Nectovia account before anything else. Sign in with your browser opens the sign-in page, and this computer keeps your sign-in in its protected storage for the next launch. Your initials at the top of the window open the account menu, with Account settings, Switch account and Sign out.

Settings > Account shows who is signed in and each business you belong to, with your role. A Business owner also sees the plan and what it includes. A Business owner or a Manager invites people with a code that works once, for seven days; a Manager can remove Employees, and only the Business owner changes roles. Join a business takes a code someone gave you.
Add a business workspace now creates the business in your Nectovia account, with you as its Business owner. It has no plan until Diomedes Systems sets one.

The Nectovia Agent now answers Home's conversation, for All projects and for each project, on Nectovia's own AI service. There's nothing to connect: it answers for a business whose plan includes the Nectovia Agent and included AI usage, as the Business plan does. For Personal work, or a business whose plan leaves it out, it says why and sends nothing.

Setup's Connect an AI service step now says the Nectovia Agent is included with Business and needs no setup. That step and Settings > Helpers on this computer no longer offer AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter or Google Vertex AI connections.

On Windows, ChatGPT can now be set up inside Nectovia, using the Codex that comes with it. In setup and in the ChatGPT row of Settings > Helpers on this computer, Sign in to ChatGPT gives you a Continue to OpenAI link to finish signing in with your browser, and Check ChatGPT connection checks the bundled Codex and your sign-in without starting any work.

Business rules are part of the Business plan. A project's instruction files, the trigger rules in Settings > Rules and a project's own trigger rules reach the work only for a business whose plan includes Business rules. Otherwise they're kept: trigger rules show read-only, and a run's instruction files are marked as not sent. Personal work gets none of them. Nectovia's own product knowledge and writing standard still go with every run.

Where Business rules reach the work, a project's instruction files now go with every conversation message, on Home and in project threads, and with each Ask and Plan, as they already did with Work and work loop runs.

Trigger rules now watch task work on every tool as well as Nectovia work loop runs. A text rule reads what Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or another tool writes for a task and can stop it before it becomes a proposal, and on Codex a rule's correction reaches the running turn.

Nectovia now holds what it writes for you to one plain-writing standard. In answers, and in a Work proposal's summary and changed Markdown and text files, it takes out long dashes between clauses, filler openings and closing offers, and a sentence it rewrites keeps every number, name, date and file name.

Settings > Account has a Reach this computer from your phone switch for each business whose plan includes Phone access. A Business owner or a Manager can turn it on, and while it's on, this computer connects out to the business's relay and is listed as online; it never listens for connections. Turning it off or signing out removes this computer's record.

On Windows the program file is now nectovia.exe, and an update removes the old Diomedes.exe from the install folder. The install folder and the data folders keep the Diomedes name, so an update still finds your projects.

sections.title: Fixed
items: In Connections, Deliver signed stock event now reaches Nectovia in the desktop app. From 0.1.8 on, the app refused every such event.
Italics inside bold text now display, and the labels along the bottom of a chart fit: whole, over two lines, or shortened with the full label on hover.
On the Board, a long task title shows two lines where there's room and the rest on hover or keyboard focus, and hovering shows what a task's age means and the default document's path.
Labels made from file names keep POS, CSV, PDF, SKU, W-2 and similar terms in capitals. A weekly brief's source tags open the file they name, in Files and when an answer quotes them.
Settings lists the tools on this computer once, as Helpers on this computer, or Engines when Interface detail is Technical.
Claude Code's model list keeps the 1M-context models that recent versions of Claude Code offer, so you can choose them.

A trigger rule edited by hand that Nectovia can't run now stops the runs it would watch, and the rule editor names it. The editor also refuses pattern rules that together would take too long to check, and says how to shorten them.

items: This build is unsigned and experimental. On Windows, SmartScreen may warn before the installer runs: choose More info, then Run anyway, after checking the file's SHA-256. The Mac build has an ad hoc signature with no Apple Developer ID and is not notarized, so the first time you open it, right-click the app and choose Open, or allow it under System Settings, Privacy and Security.
There is no build for Intel Macs, and the Apple silicon build has been built and launched only on a GitHub-hosted Mac.

Apart from one trigger rule run on Claude Code, a read-only look at its model list and a measurement of the writing standard on answers from the Claude Code command line, nothing in this version was tried against a real provider. Every route in its tests was scripted or fake, the Nectovia Agent's AI service included, and Sign in to ChatGPT was never tried against OpenAI.

Signing in, Settings > Account and the Nectovia Agent's AI service were tested only against stand-ins for the Nectovia account service and its sign-in page, and the return to the app after signing in on a Mac has not been tried. The account service this version uses is still a staging service with a fixed testing budget: while it is, the Nectovia Agent's answers are kept short, and the Agent stops answering once that budget is spent.

Signing in needs the Nectovia account service, so if it can't be reached when Nectovia starts, you can't open anything, your own projects included; the sign-in screen says why. A connection lost after you sign in doesn't sign you out.

The Nectovia Agent answers in the conversation only: Build, Fix and work loops don't run on it yet. Besides the scripted demonstration, Loop run offers only AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter and Google Vertex AI, which setup no longer connects, and Loop run is in the task's work panel, which the Conversation view hides.

The phone apps can't reach this computer through the relay yet; this version only connects the computer and lists it as online. The relay was tested against a stand-in and hasn't yet run on the live account service.
An update that installs this version over an earlier one, including the change from Diomedes.exe to nectovia.exe, hasn't been run on an installed copy.

These parts have not had an independent review: signing in and Settings > Account, the Nectovia Agent's AI service, ChatGPT setup, Business rules, the phone relay, trigger rules on task work and plain writing, and from 0.2.0, suggested edits to instruction files, playbook reading, the zoom and accessibility fixes, the Repository section, the update refresh, the Rules screens and Loop run.
Automations run the weekly brief alone, and only while this computer is on. They tell you inside the app and send nothing by push, email or phone.
Resume, Retry, Fork and Steer work on ChatGPT (Codex) runs only.
Run checks run only the checks a task declares, and never run your project's own code. Nothing checks a run automatically when it finishes.
Files has no PDF viewer. Pictures and PDFs cannot be sent to an AI, and a binary file cannot be put back from an earlier version.

Trigger rules don't watch conversations, Ask or Plan. Tool rules don't reach Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or other outside tools, which run their own tools, and on every outside tool except Codex a text rule reads the text after secrets are removed, so a rule looking for a secret may not fire there. A correction asked of a tool other than Codex was not tested, and a rule that asks a work loop run to correct still can't reach it: the correction is recorded and shown as not sent.

Helpers that take pieces of a loop run's work, each in its own copy of the files, and a lead that runs a small team of them are built but cannot be started from the app yet. The Console still has no History screen and no Make tasks from this plan.

Every route except the Nectovia Agent still runs on, and is billed to, your own account. That includes any AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter or Google Vertex AI connection you saved yourself, which now works only for a business whose plan includes the Nectovia Agent. You can still choose such a connection for a thread, and Settings no longer has a place to change or remove it.

releases.headline: Rules that act while a task runs, a work loop you start from a task, a Git view for software projects, automations, a line-by-line review of every change, and updates that refresh your install. Now also on Apple silicon Macs.

sections.title: New
items: Rule triggers. Write rules in Settings > Rules for every project, or from the Trigger rules line under Project instructions in a thread for one project or one task. A rule watches what a Nectovia work loop run writes, or the tool it is about to use on a file, and can note it, ask the run to correct, hold the step for your go-ahead before it runs, or stop and ask you. A project rule can add to or tighten a rule written for every project but never loosen it, and the app shows the reason when it refuses one. Each time a rule acts, it shows in the run's Supervision section.

Start a Nectovia work loop run on a task with Loop run in the task's work panel. It offers only the routes that are ready, asks before a route sends anything off this computer, and opens the run so you can watch it plan, act and check.

Software projects get a Repository section at the top of Files when the Software Engineering pack is on: the branch, changed files with a readable diff, and recent commits. It can add or remove a separate worktree on a new branch without touching your own checkout, and run the build and test commands you declare, asking you every time. A task whose check is one of those commands can be Verified on that result.
A Mac build for Apple silicon (M1 and later) is published beside the Windows installer.

Automations. Open Automations from the Nectovia group or Ctrl K. The weekly brief is listed there, and Run once runs it now. Owners and admins can turn on a schedule, pause it, resume it or turn it off; the screen shows the next three runs and any that were missed or skipped. Saving a schedule does not turn it on.

Review what a task changed before you keep it. A task's thread shows each change line by line, and you can keep or undo each one, keep or undo them all, or send notes back with Revise with these comments.

Approvals you give often can be remembered. After you approve the same step three times in a project, Nectovia asks whether to stop asking. Remembered approvals are listed in the Task permissions dialog, where Revoke takes any of them back.
Ready work can start by itself. A switch on the Board, off until you turn it on, starts ready tasks automatically, and Pause queue or Pause all stops that again.

Files you drop or paste into a project land in its Imports folder. Pictures, CSV files and the first sheet of an Excel file show as previews, a file's older versions can be opened, and Attach adds a file to a thread.
A run's result now says whether it was checked: Verified, Not verified, Failed verification or Verification uncertain, in the thread and on the Board, with Run checks and Verify again.
Running work has more controls. Stop options offers ways to stop a request, and Resume, Retry, Fork and a Steer box work on ChatGPT (Codex) runs.
On the Nectovia home conversation, Claude Code keeps its session between messages. While an answer is being written you can queue your next message, and Stop ends the answer cleanly.
Settings > Agent profiles saves a route, an exact model and an effort setting as a profile, and a project can list which profiles its work uses, in order.
A Context used line under replies on the AWS, Azure, OpenRouter and Google Cloud routes shows what was sent to the model and what was summarised to fit.
Project instructions now include instruction files in subfolders, and a run shows exactly which files it received, with Open in Files.
Nectovia can suggest edits to a project's instruction files. You approve or decline each one, and can roll back to before any of them.
Run details have a Supervision section that flags a run drifting away from its task.

Capability packs can be installed, turned off, updated, rolled back or uninstalled from the Task permissions dialog, including a pack from a folder on this computer. With the Small Business pack on, Ctrl K can open a playbook to read it as well as use it.
Conversation text size can be set to 90, 100, 110 or 125 percent under Settings > Appearance or from the ··· menu.
The Windows icon, the installer, the Start menu entry and the window title now say Nectovia. The install folder and the program file keep the Diomedes name, so an update still finds your projects.

Settings > What's new lists what every release changed, and after an update Nectovia shows the new version's notes once. When Check for updates finds a newer version, its notes appear before you download it.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Unsaved writing is no longer lost when you leave the editor another way, such as through Settings, Projects, another file or the command palette.
The thread header no longer shows a document's context as a percentage like 4182 percent; it shows a size.
Plan files no longer get broken names, task names no longer stop mid-thought, and the weekly brief no longer uses the whole setup sentence as its title.
Italic text displays, and each choice in the Cloud sharing dialog sits on its own line.
Stopping a tool on Windows no longer sometimes reports a clean-up failure that did not happen.
Facts in Discovery can be corrected or retired again after their source file is edited.
An installed tool that changes in place is noticed, and size limits count the real size of text in any language.
At 200 percent zoom and in small windows the work area and the inspector are usable again, and the Interface detail menu closes with Escape.
Two windows sending the first message in a new project at the same moment no longer makes one of them refuse its own message.

sections.title: Updating
items: Settings > App updates offers stable releases only. Nothing is downloaded, verified or installed until you confirm it, and a download is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the digest the release publishes. An installed 0.1.7, 0.1.8, 0.1.9, 0.1.10 or 0.1.11 on Windows can find this release when you press Check for updates.

An update from 0.1.9, 0.1.10 or 0.1.11 keeps your settings, routes, saved keys, projects and conversations. An update from 0.1.7 or 0.1.8 that skips 0.1.9 still gets the one-time fresh start 0.1.9 introduced: the earlier version's data and the Documents\Diomedes folder are set aside, renamed with "before 0.1.9" and the date, and nothing is deleted.

Your install is refreshed the first time this version opens, and again after each later update. Settings you never changed move to the new defaults, anything you chose is kept, cached screens are cleared, and a byte-for-byte backup and a record of what moved are kept. A custom look keeps its colours, fonts and artwork, while text sizes, line spacing and density follow the new version. You see it once: Updated to 0.2.0, with how many settings moved.
This is the first Mac version. On a Mac, Check for updates says when a newer version exists, and you download it from the release page; the app does not install it itself.

sections.title: Known limits
items: Unsigned and experimental. On Windows, SmartScreen may warn before the installer runs: choose More info, then Run anyway, after checking the file's SHA-256. The Mac build is signed ad hoc, not with an Apple Developer ID, and is not notarized, so the first time you open it, right-click the app and choose Open, or allow it under System Settings, Privacy and Security.
The Mac build is for Apple silicon only; there is no Intel Mac build. It was built and launched on a GitHub-hosted Mac, not on a person's computer.

Nothing in this version was tried against a real provider. Every route in its tests was scripted or fake, including Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI and OpenRouter.

Some parts are new and have not yet had an independent review: suggested edits to instruction files, playbook reading, the zoom and accessibility fixes, the Repository section, the update refresh, the Rules screens and Loop run. Rule triggers themselves were reviewed and the problems found were fixed.
Automations run only the weekly brief, only while this computer is on, and tell you only inside the app: nothing is sent by push, email or phone.
Resume, Retry, Fork and Steer work on ChatGPT (Codex) runs only. Claude Code keeps its session on the home conversation only, not in project threads.
Run checks run only the checks a task declares, and never run your project's own code. Nothing checks a run automatically when it finishes.
Files has no PDF viewer. Pictures and PDFs cannot be sent to an AI, and a binary file cannot be put back from an earlier version.

Rule triggers watch Nectovia work loop runs only. Work on Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and other outside tools is not watched, and a rule that asks a loop run to correct cannot reach it yet: the correction is recorded and shown as not sent. Loop run is in the task's work panel, which the Conversation view hides.
Helpers that take pieces of a loop run's work, each in its own copy of the files, and a lead that runs a small team of them are built but cannot be started from the app yet.
The Console still has no History screen, no Make tasks from this plan and no Stop for a conversation.
This app is not signed in to a Nectovia account, and every route runs on, and is billed to, your own account.

releases.headline: The Files list no longer stalls the app on a large project, and a conversation keeps answering when one of its earlier runs cannot be read.

sections.title: Fixed
items: The Files list no longer stalls the app on a large project. Listing a 3,000-file folder used to take about 40 seconds. It now takes well under a second, and a link, junction or private name is still refused exactly as before.

A conversation keeps answering when one of its earlier runs cannot be read, for example after a damaged file or a downgrade. Before, every new message on that thread was refused. Now the thread says once that it won't remember the part it couldn't read, and carries on; the unreadable file is left as it is.
Settings no longer accept the keys the retired Workbook used. Nothing in the app sends them; a settings file from an older build still loses them when it loads.
Everything else is 0.1.10.

releases.headline: This release starts over: the first time it opens, it sets aside what the earlier version kept and opens as a new install.

sections.title: New
items: This release starts over. The first time 0.1.9 opens on a computer that had an earlier version, it sets aside everything the earlier version kept: its settings, its list of projects, its routes and their saved keys, its conversations, the saved account sign-in and the Documents\Diomedes projects folder. Nothing is deleted. Each is renamed with "before 0.1.9" and the date in its name, next to where it was, so a file can still be found by hand. Nectovia then opens as a new install. This happens once.

Installed tools are accepted at whatever version they report. Claude Code, OpenCode, Oh My Pi, Cursor and Devin are no longer held to one reviewed version, so a tool that updated itself is not called incompatible. A tool that cannot report its version at all is still refused. A Claude Code conversation carries on after Claude Code updates.
When Check this computer finds nothing Nectovia can use, it says so: "No available engines found. Install a compatible one below."
The Workbook is gone. The Console is the only way to work in a project.

The Console has two views, chosen from the detail menu. Conversation shows the message box and the threads; Architect shows the whole Console. A new person lands in Conversation when setup finishes. A view changes what is shown, never what Nectovia can do.
A thread's menu has "Update this conversation". It asks first, then starts each open conversation whose instructions are older than this build over on today's, and a note in the thread says so.
Each artifact in an answer is recorded with a fingerprint of its content, and the thread can show that record. An artifact whose message is gone shows as "No longer in the conversation".
A Markdown or Mermaid file a model writes is refused if it begins with HTML, so opening it from disk in a browser cannot run anything in it. Files you write or save yourself are unchanged.

releases.headline: The app calls itself Nectovia, answers appear as they are written, and work styles choose where work runs.

sections.title: New
items: The app calls itself Nectovia. Its screens, its home page and its answers use the new name. The installer, the Start menu entry, the window title, the Documents\Diomedes projects folder and the release files keep the Diomedes name, so this build upgrades an earlier experimental install in place and finds your projects where they were.

A new install opens on the Nectovia look: ink and cyan, a home page that opens with the date, a greeting and a row for each of your projects. An update keeps the look you already had. To switch, choose Nectovia under Settings > Appearance.

Answers appear as they are written, on the Nectovia page and in project threads, and a line under the answer names each tool call while it runs, such as a web search. Not every route reports its tool calls.

Work styles choose where work runs. Pick Efficient, Focused or Thorough from the style control in a thread or on the Nectovia page, and the tier map in Settings > Engines > Tiers decides the route and the model. As shipped, Efficient runs GPT-5.6 Luna on AWS Bedrock and Focused runs Gemini 3.8 Flash on Google Vertex AI, each on your own account. Thorough has no model until you choose one there. A tier whose route is not connected is refused by name, and its work never moves to another provider.

Each job on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI or OpenRouter has a cap: 20 credits for Efficient, 50 for Focused and 100 for Thorough. A job stops before the step that would pass its cap, and nothing more is spent. On the Nectovia page the app asks before sending a message that is likely to pass its cap.

Google Vertex AI is a new route, set up in Settings > Engines. Azure OpenAI and OpenRouter can be connected there too, with your own keys and the prices you declare. AWS Bedrock is set up as before and now streams its answers.
The OpenCode route reads your OpenCode model list as it is now, gives each readiness check at most five seconds, and shows the answer without the model's reasoning.

Answers can carry artifacts. A diagram, an image, a design or a document opens in a side panel from a chip under the answer, and a table is drawn in the answer itself. Ask and Plan answers can also draw charts, figures and progress bars in place. In a project, the panel saves to Files under Saved artifacts.

Each project has a Cloud sharing button in its top bar. A new project shares nothing: every route except the sample is refused until you tick it there. The same dialog chooses each document a route may read and whether earlier messages may be sent.
Ask and Plan can look things up. Helper routes can search and read the web, and Claude Code can look through the project folder for one message when you tick that box before sending.
The local service answers only this app's own window. Another program on this computer, or a web page in your browser, is refused.
A Small Business pack of twelve playbooks can be turned on for a project from Ctrl K. Using a playbook fills the composer with a prepared Ask or Plan request.

This app is not signed in to a Nectovia account. No credit balance or usage is shown, and every route runs on, and is billed to, your own account.

releases.headline: The Diomedes page is now a durable conversation, and AWS Bedrock can be connected on your own account.

sections.title: New
items: The Diomedes page is now a durable conversation. All projects has its own conversation, and each project has its own Diomedes thread. Each is created on your first message and kept after that; opening the page creates nothing.

A conversation without a route you chose yourself runs on AWS Bedrock (GPT-5.6 Luna). A route you chose is kept, and you can choose another available route. Work a conversation starts still needs an explicit project and the same approvals as before.
Stop requests an end to the turn you sent. A stop the app cannot confirm is shown as unconfirmed, and provider charges already incurred may remain.

In Settings, find AWS Bedrock (GPT-5.6 Luna). Enter your AWS account number and your Bedrock API key yourself, confirm what may be sent to AWS Bedrock under that account, and press Connect AWS. Then approve a spend limit and press Save limit. The app's estimated limit is not a cap enforced by AWS billing. The key is saved using the desktop app's protected storage.

sections.title: Updating
items: Settings > App updates offers stable releases only. Nothing is downloaded, verified or installed until you confirm it, and a download is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the digest the release publishes. An installed earlier version can find this release when you press Check for updates. The build remains experimental and unsigned.

sections.title: Known limits
items: Connections is unavailable in the app and opens no screen. There is no live connection to a business system in this release.
The AWS account, its access, its credits and its bill belong to the person who sets it up. This release includes no AWS access, and there is no automatic fallback to another provider.
Replies appear after they complete.
No live provider call was made in this release, and every provider in its tests was scripted or fake. Nobody has installed this build on a clean customer machine and connected AWS end to end.
The release is Windows x64 only. A public upgrade from an older customer installation has not been exercised end to end.

releases.headline: The Console is one screen language, and Setup can repair an installation it cannot use.

sections.title: New
items: The Console is one screen language. Home, the strip across the top, the Everything rail and History were rebuilt so spacing, corner radius, motion and colour are decided in one place. History is a screen inside the Console now, and there is an editor for a task document.

Every dropdown in the app is drawn by the app, so a menu no longer opens in the app's colours and closes in the system's. How a dropdown behaves did not change: it is still reachable from the keyboard and still read by a screen reader.

The Projects view lets you choose how a question runs. The mode sits beside the question with a line naming what that mode is allowed to do, and it travels with the question. If the project you pick has no thread yet, one is opened for the question.

Discovery and Readiness are screens you can open. Discovery records a prospect's inputs, hand-offs and time, takes an owner's correction on a recorded fact, and imports a research brief. Readiness shows which tools are available and what each workflow still needs. Neither screen needs a Business account.

Setup can repair an installation it cannot use. A wrong-version, changed or corrupt installation now offers to repair itself with a compatible copy, and a missing one offers to install that copy. Claude Code, OpenCode and oh-my-pi have such a copy; Cursor and Devin do not.

Setup also offers a connection test you press yourself. It says what it will do before it does it: one small synthetic request through the route you chose, which may use that service's allowance or add provider charges. It is sent once rather than retried.
The app ships what it knows about itself, so an answer about how Diomedes works comes from the build you are running.

sections.title: Updating
items: Settings > App updates offers stable releases only. Nothing is downloaded, verified or installed until you confirm it, and a download is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the digest the release publishes. An installed 0.1.5 is offered this build when you press Check for updates.

sections.title: Known limits
items: Unsigned, experimental, one machine tested.
Every Claude Code text request still starts a fresh process, so a follow-up is a new request and nothing is resumed.
Organisation access is in this build as groundwork with no screen, so there is no multi-user behaviour to see.
Durable inventory stock receipts are in this build, but no screen shows them.

In an ordinary install you can open the Design Center, change things and watch the preview, while Apply, Save as new theme and Import do not work, and the screen says so.

releases.headline: This build adds reviewed foundations for sign-in, inventory and workforce planning.

sections.title: New
items: Adds the reviewed account-service and native sign-in prerequisites, including protected credential storage and packaged sign-in support.
Adds reviewed inventory contracts, catalog and import preparation and stock-command calculations for later integration into authorized workflows.
Adds workforce proposal constraints and scoped outcome-evidence calculations.
Improves local durable-event recovery.

sections.title: Known limits
items: This is an experimental Windows build. The application and installer are unsigned.
Native sign-in still requires the deployed identity configuration and provider and Windows qualification before it can be offered as a working customer sign-in flow.
Inventory, scheduling and value calculations are prerequisites; this release does not enable autonomous purchasing, guest messaging, kitchen devices or a complete restaurant workflow.
The personalized meeting displays remain labeled concepts.
Local event recovery does not certify remote tenancy or provider reconnection.

releases.headline: The Files pane works from the keyboard, and streaming answers now belong to the run that produced them.

sections.title: New
items: The Files pane works from the keyboard. The file tree takes a single tab stop and moves under the arrow keys, Home and End, with Enter and Space to open a file. Back returns focus to the row you came from.

A preview that fails to load now offers an explicit retry instead of leaving an empty panel. The pane keeps its state per project, so switching projects no longer carries the previous project's open folders and selection across.

Streaming answers now belong to the run that produced them. Before this build, text from a cancelled or taken-over attempt could still arrive and paint over a newer answer. If the connection drops, the app throws the partial text away and re-reads the saved answer.
Cursor and Devin now run through one shared implementation. Nothing about how you use either route changed.

A dropped connection mid-answer now produces exactly one outcome. The app records a single result that needs reconciling, invents no completion, and still shows that same single result after a restart.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Deep folder hierarchies no longer widen the Files pane past its own scroll container.
A slow preview that lost its race is discarded rather than painting over the file you are looking at now.

sections.title: Updating
items: Settings > App updates offers stable releases only. Nothing is downloaded, verified or installed until you confirm it, and a download is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the digest the release publishes. An installed 0.1.3 is offered this build when you press Check for updates.

sections.title: Known limits
items: Unsigned, experimental, one machine tested.
Live streaming text is never replayed. If you lose the connection while a model is writing, you see the finished answer when it lands, not the part you missed. This is a deliberate limit.

releases.headline: This build adds the Design Center, which changes how Diomedes looks with the real screens previewing live beside the controls.

sections.title: New
items: This build adds the Design Center: Settings > Design Center > Open Design Center. It changes how Diomedes looks - colours, type, spacing, corner radius, motion, and imported pictures - with the real screens previewing live beside the controls. It needs no internet connection, no account and no AI engine, and it sends nothing anywhere.

Appearance work is included in a Diomedes Business subscription and is done by our own design team: we build and install your first look after a design consultation, and up to two revisions a year are included. You do not have to author it yourself, and there is no add-on to buy.

Nothing about appearance costs money to undo. Built-in schemes, text size, zoom, contrast, reduced motion, texture off, focus visibility and the safe reset are free and always work; Settings > Appearance > any built-in scheme puts everything back.
A theme is data, never a plug-in. Imported pictures must be PNG, JPEG or WebP; SVG is refused with a sentence.
Applying a theme does not restart anything. The app changes colour where it stands; unsent messages, scroll position and running work are untouched.
A theme that will not load is not a broken app. Diomedes falls back to the last version that worked, then to the built-in package, and says which one you are looking at.
Themes are private to the account and workspace they were made in.
If you never open it, nothing changes for you except one new Design Center entry in the Settings list on desktop.
